title: Pre-Market — Wednesday Nov 11, 2026
html:
Chips rip on CoreWeave, and SPY gaps right up to its next ceiling. Here's what I'm seeing before the bell. Yesterday's hot inflation scare is being bought back, led by AI chips, but the gap lands SPY on a level where sellers showed up before.

The one thing

SPY is at $756.49 pre-market, 68 cents under the $757.17 ceiling. That's also target 1 for the open SPY $775 call.

Why it matters: CoreWeave's strong quarter flipped the AI mood overnight, so the gap is real money, not noise. But $757.17 (half of the Oct–Nov drop) is where the bounce has stalled. Above it, SPY has room to $762–765. Rejected there, a pullback to $751.39 is normal. Either way, the plan is to take profit on the SPY call at target 1, not to buy more here.

Overnight in plain words

  • Futures: S&P 500 about +0.7%, Nasdaq 100 about +1.6%, Dow about flat. SPY trades +0.9% and QQQ +1.9% pre-market.
  • Asia and Europe: Chip markets rebounded hard: Taiwan +3.6%, South Korea +2.4%, Japan's Nikkei +1.3%. Hong Kong −1.0%, Shanghai +0.5%. Europe is edging higher.
  • Oil: Up again. WTI about $87.08 (+1.2%), Brent about $93.25 (+2.0%), after a report that a tanker hit a naval mine in the Strait of Hormuz. Good for XOM, a headwind for DAL and RCL.
  • Rates and fear: The 10-year Treasury yield sits near 5.0% after jumping 0.11 points on CPI day. The bond market is closed today for Veterans Day, so yields won't move much until Thursday. The VIX, the market's fear gauge, closed at 19.46: calm.
  • Headlines: CoreWeave (an AI cloud company) beat on revenue ($3.66B vs $3.55B expected) and raised its 2026 outlook; its stock is up about 13%. Markets price roughly a 90% chance the Fed raises rates a quarter point on Dec 9.

SPY at the open (SPY)

Ladder levels:

  • $781.62 — Oct 6 record high
  • $761–765 — Ceiling · 61.8% + 20- & 50-day
  • $757.17 — 50% of the drop · call target 1
  • $751.39 — 38.2% · first support
  • $744–745 — The floor · old floor + 23.6%
  • $732.71 — Nov 5 low · call stop $732
  • $722–728 — 200-day + 38.2% of the big run
  • $703.87 — 50% of the Mar–Oct run
  • $756.49 — pre-market
  • If SPY opens above $757.17… the ceiling gave way. That's target 1 for the SPY $775 call: the plan is to take the profit there (my estimate of the call is about $650–670 vs the $450.50 entry; check the live mid). Next stop for SPY is $762–765.
  • If it holds between $751.39 and $757.17… the gap is holding but stuck under the ceiling. Hold the call, keep the $732 stop, and let price come to $757.17. No new SPY buys inside this box.
  • If it opens below $751.39… the gap is fading. The call stays on while SPY is above $745, but don't add. Under $744, the floor is cracking and we review the call.

Movers on your list (Watchlist)

  • PLTR $172.93 +2.4%: Pre-market it's above the $172.23 call trigger. Closer to triggering, but a pre-market print doesn't count: it needs to hold above $172.23 after the open. Catch: the $180 call likely costs about $835 now, over the $800 limit (my estimate; verify). See the plays check for the backup strike.
  • NVDA $175.19 +3.7%: Back above the 1.382 extension ($174.12) that capped it yesterday. Earnings are Nov 17 and puts were EXPENSIVE. No change: watch only.
  • DELL $360.00 +7.7%: Back above its 200-day average ($338.91). The downside idea (watching $295) is off for now; it would need DELL back under $338.91 to come back. Earnings Nov 24.
  • SMH $505.55 +4.5%: The chip fund jumps but stays under its 200-day ($522.62). The downside idea ($427, then below $400) is further away; no change, no play.
  • MU · AMD · SMCI · DRAM +6–8%: MU $772.73 (+6.6%, back over its 200-day $759.88), AMD $547.64 (+6.3%), SMCI $29.53 (+6.3%), DRAM $43.85 (+7.9%). The CoreWeave effect. No plays: gaps this big are for watching, not chasing.
  • BE $201.41 +8.6%: Bouncing inside your levels: above the 0.786 ($156.28), still well under the 1.382 ($227.97). No change.

Quiet: DAL $91.96 (−0.3%; the open call and its $83 stop are unchanged), BA $173.80 (+0.2%), RCL $339.76 (flat; its options are still too thin), HLT $379.99 (flat), SPCX $147.89 (+3.4%), TSLA $386.95 (+1.9%), KO $95.75 (−1.2%, money leaving the safe names), XOM $165.20 (+0.4%, between your 1.618 at $159.09 and 2.0 at $166.89).

Today's calendar

  • Data: 7:00 a.m.: mortgage applications rose 6.2% last week (already out). 11:00 a.m.: LSEG/Ipsos consumer sentiment (prior 45.2). Nothing big.
  • Holiday: Veterans Day: stocks trade a full day to 4:00 p.m., but the bond market is closed. Volume can be lighter than usual.
  • Fed: Goolsbee, Musalem, Bowman, Hammack and Daly speak this week (check exact times). After a hot CPI, any talk of a bigger December hike can knock tech.
  • Earnings: No watchlist name reports today or tonight, so no IV-crush risk tonight (IV crush = option prices dropping once the news is out). Thursday after the close: Cisco and Applied Materials (AMAT moves SMH). NVDA reports Nov 17, DELL Nov 24.

Plays check (Options Playbook)

  • SPY Dec 18 $775 call · OPEN: At target 1. IV 13% vs moves 15% → CHEAP. Entry $450.50, last night's mark $480. With SPY at $756.49, I estimate about $660 (delta 0.28; verify). Target 1 is $757 → take the profit. Stop: SPY below $732. (OI 71,962 · vol 28,781 · bid/ask $4.77/$4.83 (last close))
  • PLTR Dec 18 $180 call · WATCHING: Closer, but over budget. IV 49% vs moves 50% → FAIR. PLTR is above the $172.23 trigger pre-market. If it holds after the open, the $180 call is likely ~$835 (estimate), over $800. Backup: the Dec 18 $185 call, closed $5.00, est. ~$650 now, delta 0.34, IV 48% vs moves 50% → FAIR. Same exit (a close below $158) and targets ($182.77, then $185.5–190). ($180 C: OI 8,486 · vol 542 · bid/ask $6.45/$6.65 · $185 C: OI 15,049 · bid/ask $4.90/$5.10 (last close; check today's volume))
  • DAL Dec 18 $90 call · OPEN: Still valid. IV 39% vs moves 37% → FAIR. DAL $91.96. Entry $632.50, marked $607.50 last night, about $595 now (estimate). Higher oil is the risk to watch. Target 2 $95.18; stop DAL below $83. (OI 3,138 · vol 76 · bid/ask $5.90/$6.25 (last close))
  • HLT Dec 18 $380 call · OPEN: Still valid. IV 25% vs moves 24% → FAIR. HLT $379.99, flat in very thin trading. Marked $1,290. Target 1 $385.93; exit on a close below $359.41. Thin options: sell only with a limit order near the mid. (OI 280 · vol 2 · bid/ask $11.30/$14.50 (last close; fails the liquidity rule for new money))
  • BA Dec 18 $170 put · WATCHING: Wait. IV 33% vs moves 36% → FAIR. BA $173.80, nowhere near the trigger. Enter below $165, or on a failed rally into $179–181.5. Exit above $185; targets $156.34, $147.61. (OI 4,109 · vol 217 · bid/ask $5.30/$5.60 (last close))

No new plays: the overnight move created gaps, not fresh setups. Options don't trade pre-market, so contract prices are last night's close plus my estimates; check Webull before acting.

Alerts for today

  • SPY — price crosses above $757.17 → target 1 for the $775 call; take-profit zone
  • SPY — price crosses below $751.39 → the gap is fading; no adds, $744 next
  • PLTR — price crosses above $172.23 → call trigger; if the $180 call is over $800, use the $185 call
  • BA — price crosses below $165.00 → put trigger for the $170 put
  • DAL — price crosses above $95.18 → target 2 for the open $90 call, take profit

An alert means look now, not buy now.

Opening rule of the day

Don't chase a gap into resistance. SPY is gapping straight into $757.17 and the chip names are up 5–8% before the bell. Gaps like this often give some back in the first 30 minutes. So: no new buys before 10:00. For PLTR, the trigger counts only if it's still above $172.23 after the first 15–30 minutes. For the SPY call, a limit sell at the mid is fine once $757.17 trades. Spreads are widest in the first minutes, so use limit orders, never market.

Sources: Webull pre-market snapshots and option quotes; TipRanks: Stock market today, Nov 11; Saxo: Market Quick Take, Nov 11; XTB: Morning wrap, Nov 11; Upstox: Futures hint positive opening. Pre-market prices from Webull as of about 7:15 a.m. ET.

Education, not personalized investment advice. Claude never places trades; check every quote in Webull before acting.
